activities.caption: place the conversational pressure on the scale
activities.name: spPressurePlace

config.prompt: For conversational loudness, exhalation is metered against the closed-ish larynx at what level, in centimetres of water?
config.why: Roughly 5–10 cm of water — which is why breath support is the first thing assessed in voice disorders, and why Parkinson's typically presents as a fading, whispered voice.

activities.anchor: snap shut and reopen in a rapid cycle
activities.caption: pair the facts of the sound source
activities.name: spLarynxMatch

config.prompt: Five facts of the sound source — pair them:

pairs.right: rocks the cricoid cartilage to stretch the folds — raising pitch
slacken and bulge the folds — lowering pitch
the repetition rate of the buzz — near 100 Hz for a typical adult male, 200 Hz for an adult female, 300 Hz and above for a child
/s/, /f/ and /t/ skip the buzz entirely — pure turbulence
elastic recoil plus Bernoulli suction — a self-sustaining oscillation

config.why: Pitch is controlled by tension, not airflow — a whisper carries the airflow and no pitch at all, which is the cleanest proof the two are different controls.

activities.anchor: The velum (soft palate) is a valve
activities.caption: file each feature under its axis
activities.name: spConsonantSort

config.prompt: File each feature under the axis it classifies:
config.why: The articulators sculpt constrictions that classify every consonant on three axes at once — the tongue, star of the ensemble, does the fine shaping.

config.text: The glottal buzz is rich in %%0%% — energy at the fundamental and at every whole-number multiple of it. What the ear uses for vowel identity is mostly the first two formants: %%1%% falls as the tongue lowers and the jaw opens; %%2%% falls as the tongue retracts. /i/ in "see" has low F1 around %%3%% Hz, while /a/ in "father" has high F1 around %%4%% Hz.
config.hint: A plural, two labels, two frequencies.

activities.caption: find the faulty line — source versus filter
activities.name: spFilterSpot

config.prompt: One line of this summary is wrong — click it:
lines: The larynx's output is one buzzing source.
Everything that differentiates sounds happens in the tract above.
After a laryngectomy, an electrolarynx can supply the missing source.
A gorgeous singing voice can repair distorted vowels, since the information rides in the source.
The differentiating information lives in the filter, not the source.
config.correction: Distorted vowels stay distorted regardless of voice quality — the differentiating information is the tract's shape, the filter.
config.why: The larynx makes essentially one thing; the shape of the tract above it does the differentiating.

activities.anchor: Hearing is tested by frequency and loudness
activities.caption: drag between the two halves of speech
activities.name: spVowelCompare

config.prompt: Drag between the two halves of the speech signal:

before.label: Vowels
before.text: low and loud, comparatively robust — in age-related loss they arrive while the rest goes.

after.label: Consonants
after.text: the intelligibility workhorses — /s/, /f/, /th/ and /k/ live high, where presbycusis slopes down first; 'everyone mumbles' means vowels arrive, consonants do not.

config.why: The audiogram is the map of what the ear can deliver — and intelligibility leans hard on the high end.

activities.anchor: hearing loss just means the world is quieter
activities.caption: bet before you read on — the hearing-aid paradox
activities.name: spAidPredict

config.q: In sensorineural damage, why do patients say 'I can hear you but not understand you'?
choices: The aid's amplification is too weak
The cochlea is not merely turned down but distorted — tuning blurred, loudness tolerance reduced
The patient misunderstands their own audiogram
Aids only work for the conductive kind
config.why: The aid is a prosthetic of a damaged organ, not a volume knob on a working one — amplification helps most in quiet rooms and least in noise.

activities.anchor: Diagnosis in speech therapy is locating the broken link
activities.caption: walk three referrals down the chain
activities.name: spChainBranch

config.root: Three referrals, three walks down the chain:

start.text: A patient's voice fades to a whisper across all sounds. Which stage?

choices.label: Respiration and phonation — rebuild the pressure and loudness (the Lee Silverman approach for Parkinson's)

mis1.text: All the articulators downstream are intact — the fading loudness points upstream to the power supply.

ok1.text: Next: distorted vowels and wildly inconsistent errors. Which stage?

choices.label: The audiogram — route to audiology first

mis2.text: The audiogram matters when hearing fails; wildly inconsistent errors with intact hearing point to motor planning.

ok2.text: Last: a child cannot produce /s/ but hears the difference. Articulation or phonological?

choices.label: Articulation — the target is heard, just not yet made
Phonological — the difference itself is not heard

mis3.text: Not this child — hearing the difference is exactly what they can do; the two want entirely different therapies.

ok3.text: One who cannot hear the difference has a phonological problem — different intervention entirely. And a flat, severe audiogram routes the case to audiology first: nothing runs on a signal the ear never delivers.

config.why: The sciences are the diagnostic instrument; treatment is what you do once the instrument has spoken.
